stem: A hospital tracks measures such as patient falls and hospital-acquired pressure injuries to evaluate aspects of nursing care quality. These measures are best described as:

options.A: Physician-sensitive indicators that primarily measure medical decision-making
options.B: Nursing-sensitive indicators that reflect structures, processes, or outcomes affected by nursing care
options.C: Unstructured observations that are not used for quality measurement
options.D: Billing indicators used only for reimbursement

rationale: Nursing-sensitive indicators are measures used to link nursing care with patient or system outcomes. ANA literature defines nursing-sensitive indicators as measures reflecting the structure, process, and outcomes of nursing care; falls and pressure injuries are established examples. B is correct.
educational_objective: Identify nursing-sensitive quality indicators and their relationship to nursing care and quality improvement.
source_organization: American Nurses Association (ANA); Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_document_title: Building Linkages between Nursing Care and Improved Patient Outcomes; Nursing and Patient Safety
source_version_date: ANA/OJIN 2013 foundational definition; AHRQ PSNet current page accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: ANA/OJIN definition of nursing-sensitive indicators as measures of nursing structure/process/outcomes; AHRQ PSNet Safety and Quality Rating Systems — falls and pressure ulcers as nursing-sensitive care markers
source_claim_supported: Nursing-sensitive indicators reflect nursing structures/processes/outcomes; falls and pressure injuries are examples used to assess nursing care quality and patient safety.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — quality improvement, performance improvement, and evaluation of care
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — nursing-sensitive quality indicators

source_original.stem: A hospital tracks specific quality indicators, such as fall rates and pressure injury incidence, that are considered directly influenced by nursing care, and a physician colleague assumes these numbers mainly reflect medical rather than nursing decisions. These are instead known as:

options.A: Physician-sensitive indicators that primarily measure medical decisions rather than nursing care
options.B: Nurse-sensitive indicators that reflect outcomes influenced by nursing care and nursing practice
options.C: Unstructured measurements that lack defined methods for comparing quality across clinical units
options.D: Billing indicators used primarily for reimbursement and not for clinical quality improvement

source_original.rationale: Nurse-sensitive quality indicators (such as fall rates, pressure injury incidence, and hospital-acquired infection rates) are outcome measures considered to be directly influenced by the quantity or quality of nursing care, used to evaluate and improve nursing practice and patient safety.
source_original.source_detail: Nurse-sensitive indicators are outcomes influenced by nursing care, including falls and pressure injuries; reviewed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Replaced the generic ANA homepage with an ANA/OJIN definition and AHRQ patient-safety corroboration. Corrected the overstatement that indicators are necessarily 'directly' caused by nursing quantity/quality; final wording uses affected/sensitive to nursing care. Reduced difficulty from hard to easy.

audit_findings.source_authority: ANA/OJIN foundational measure definition plus AHRQ PSNet; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: AHRQ current patient-safety page checked 2026-08-17; no conflicting current definition identified.
audit_findings.claim_audit: ANA defines nursing-sensitive indicators as measures reflecting nursing structure, process and outcomes; AHRQ identifies falls/pressure ulcers as markers of nursing care quality.

distractor_audit.A: Misclassifies measures specifically linked to nursing care.
distractor_audit.C: Quality indicators are structured measures, not unstructured observations.
distractor_audit.D: They serve quality/safety assessment, not only billing.

audit_findings.cueing: Removed physician-colleague narrative and direct answer phrase from the stem.
audit_findings.blueprint: Quality/performance evaluation fits Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked ANA definition and AHRQ examples; B remains uniquely defensible.
